sources.entry: Requestly - A lightweight open-source API Development, Testing & Mocking platform

summary.one_liner: Requestly API Client is a closed-source desktop API client (REST, GraphQL) whose GitHub repo serves as the community hub for bug reports, feature requests, and the roadmap.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes the Requestly API Client, a proprietary application for designing, building, and testing APIs, with local, team-sync, or self-hosted data storage. Listed features include saving and testing REST requests, pre- and post-request scripts, import/export of cURL, Postman, and OpenAPI contracts, GraphQL testing with schema introspection and auto-completion, Git sync of collections, and local workspaces stored as files. Downloads are offered for macOS (Apple Silicon and Intel), Windows, and Linux. This repository itself does not contain the application source; it is used for issues, feature requests, questions, and roadmap. The README also states that the older open-source browser extension and web app moved to requestly/interceptor.
use_cases: test REST and GraphQL APIs locally
import Postman collections or OpenAPI specs
keep API collections in a Git repository
run pre- and post-request scripts on API calls
report bugs or request features for Requestly API Client
how_to_run: Download the installer for your platform from the Download section of the README (macOS Apple Silicon or Intel, Windows, Linux).
stack: Proprietary desktop application (technology not named in README)
notable: Git-native collections synced with a Git repository
Import/export from cURL, Postman, and OpenAPI
Local-only workspaces with no cloud storage required
Free for up to 10 collaborators; paid Team and Enterprise tiers add SSO, SAML, audit logs, on-prem deployment
caveats: The API Client application is closed-source and proprietary; this repo is not its source code
Team and Enterprise tiers add SSO, SAML, audit logs, and on-prem deployment at a cost; free tier is limited to 10 collaborators
The open-source HTTP Interceptor code has moved to requestly/interceptor
summary.license: GNU AGPLv3 for the repository content; the API Client application itself is proprietary
keywords: desktop api client mac windows linux
